title: The Ternary Operator
instructions: The ternary operator is a tiny if/else squeezed into one line.
So (age >= 18) ? "adult" : "minor" gives "adult" when age is 18 or more, otherwise "minor".
It's handy for picking between two values quickly. Don't overuse it — a normal if is clearer for anything complex.
task: Fill in the ternary so age 20 prints:  You are an adult
hint:
Write the condition, then ? true-value : false-value:

    char *result = (age >= 18) ? "adult" : "minor";
